added_models.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)

engagement.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: Studies 34885_IVHU and TR003 are undated in the review; the clone-selection design (TAB001 clones 38 and 41 against nivolumab) places them before the 2016 phase 1. The circulating-cell null is 'data not shown'.
engagement.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
engagement.note: Toripalimab raised splenic CD3+/CD4+/CD8+ frequencies and effector-memory share in PBMC-engrafted NSG mice; circulating frequencies unchanged (data not shown). No patient comparison.
engagement.short: Splenic T-cell expansion in PBMC mice
engagement.quote: Treatment with toripalimab increased T cell numbers compared to isotype control (Figure 7, upper panel).
engagement.reason: Splenic readout has no patient counterpart
engagement.judgement: Opened as its own track per the checker's missing list: the review files two PBMC-engrafted NSG studies (34885_IVHU, TR003) that none of the draft's toripalimab tracks carries. The nearest patient PD readout is Tang 2019 (NCT02836795): 'There was no major impact of JS001 on the frequency of activated CD8+ T lymphocytes in the peripheral blood in individual subjects.' That agrees with the mouse's own circulating null (data not shown) but is an activation fraction in blood, not the lineage frequency in spleen the model reported, so it is not scored: not same (the headline splenic readout has no human counterpart) and not contra (the compartment the model reported unchanged was also unchanged in patients). A checker who takes the blood null as the comparison would score same at low confidence. Downstream tier: cell numbers, not occupancy.

efficacy.confidence_note: Year is a proxy as in the engagement cell; Study TR003 is undated in the review and the reviewer gives no tumour growth inhibition number, only 'minor antitumor activity'.
efficacy.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
efficacy.note: In Study TR003, toripalimab had minor antitumor activity against MC38 in NSG mice engrafted with allogeneic anti-624Mel CD8 CTLs; no melanoma tumour, no patient comparison.
efficacy.short: Minor MC38 activity with allogeneic CTLs
efficacy.quote: Engraftment of T cells alone had no antitumor activity and toripalimab (10 mg i.p. twice weekly) had minor antitumor activity in T cell-engrafted mice harboring allogeneic T cells (Figure 8).
efficacy.judgement: The filed efficacy arm of this system is odd: a mouse colon tumour (MC38) in NSG mice given allogeneic human CD8 CTLs raised against B7-1-transfected 624Mel melanoma cells, so the T cells were not tumour-specific and the effect was minor. Nobody had compared it with patients at this date; toripalimab's own melanoma comparison in the draft sits on the knock-in MC38 track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: qualitative 'minor antitumor activity' of toripalimab in MC38/allogeneic-CTL NSG mice vs RECIST objective response rate 17.3%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Tang 2020 (Clin Cancer Res, paywalled; quote confirmed verbatim by the checker on the draft's entry). The model side is qualitative ('minor antitumor activity', no TGI number) in a non-melanoma tumour with non-specific allogeneic T cells, so the pairing is weak. NCT03013101 has no posted results.
efficacy.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
efficacy.note: POLARIS-01 met its ORR primary (17.3%, 128 Chinese patients, acral/mucosal-heavy); the allogeneic-CTL NSG arm had predicted only minor toripalimab activity.
efficacy.short: Modest ORR after minor mouse activity
efficacy.quote: Among 127 patients assessed, 1 complete response, 21 partial response, and 51 stable disease were observed for objective response rate of 17.3% and disease control rate of 57.5%.

patient_trials.quote: The primary objective was safety and objective response rate.

efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: no source puts the T-cell-engrafted NSG study beside POLARIS-01. The model made a weak positive prediction for toripalimab and the single-arm ORR primary was met (China conditional approval December 2018, publication April 2020 is the earliest public comparison), so direction agreed and the muted magnitude is of a piece with 'minor'. Scored same at low confidence rather than left untested because the brief scores any directional agreement; a checker who regards the allogeneic-CTL arm as too far from a melanoma prediction would keep this cell untested until the 2023 pucotenlimab entry.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HCC827 xenograft tumour growth inhibition in PBMC-engrafted NSG mice vs RECIST objective response rate 20.17% (different metrics)
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text for both papers (PMC7153830, PMC9901108). The MiXeno tumour was a lung adenocarcinoma xenograft (HCC827), not melanoma. No NMPA review is public, so whether the model was filed is unknown. The mAbs DOI resolves (tandfonline returns 403 to scripted requests; confirmed through PMC).
efficacy.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
efficacy.note: Pucotenlimab (HX008) inhibited HCC827 growth in PBMC-engrafted NSG mice (Zhang 2020); its melanoma phase 2 (119 patients, 52% acral) met its ORR primary at 20.2%.
efficacy.quote: As the lower limit of the 95% CI of actual ORR exceeded the threshold of 10%, the primary endpoint of this study was reached.

patient_trials.quote: The primary endpoint was ORR assessed by IRC based on RECIST v1.1.

efficacy.reason: HX008 MiXeno activity; melanoma ORR primary met
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Cui 2023 never mentions the mouse work, and Zhang 2020 (mAbs) predates the melanoma result (trial start 2018-11-08; ORR first public with the 2023 paper; registry record posted 2021-02-11, no results posted), so this is a prospective prediction, not a retrodiction. The draft's efficacy judgement says pucotenlimab 'has no published pre-clinic model'; Zhang 2020 is that model: 'In both models, HX008 significantly inhibits tumor growth and shows an effective antitumor response comparable to approved anti-PD-1 drugs.' Only the PBMC MiXeno arm is this system; the HuGEMM human-PD-1 knock-in MC38 arm is the same system as the draft's tori-hpd1-knockin-mc38-mouse track and is listed under considered_not_added. Second member drug on the track, hence strengthens. Direction only: TGI in a lung xenograft against melanoma ORR, and the subtype gradient (cutaneous 36%, acral 16%, mucosal 9%) is nothing the model carried.

added_models.model: Humanised-PD-1 C57BL/6 mouse with S180 homografts, 124I-toripalimab immuno-PET

engagement.confidence_note: Open-access full text (PMC7452040). The mice were Junshi's humanised-PD-1 C57BL/6 strain, the same strain as the filed knock-in MC38 efficacy model, but the tracer, tumour (S180 sarcoma homograft) and readout (PET biodistribution) differ, so it is opened as its own track; the checker may fold it into tori-hpd1-knockin-mc38-mouse. The FDA review never mentions the PET work. Isotope superscripts are rendered inline in the quote (124I).
engagement.model: Humanised-PD-1 C57BL/6 mouse with S180 homografts, 124I-toripalimab immuno-PET
engagement.note: 124I-labelled toripalimab accumulated in S180 tumours of humanised-PD-1 mice above IgG and cold-blocked controls; no human imaging yet.
engagement.short: Tracer uptake in hPD-1 mouse tumours
engagement.quote: Immuno-PET imaging showed that the uptake in the tumor area of the 124I-JS001 group at different time points was significantly higher than that of the blocking group or the 124I-hIgG group in the humanized PD1 mouse model.
engagement.judgement: A target-imaging system no draft track carries: clinical-grade 124I-toripalimab, validated in vitro on PHA-activated T cells, then imaged in humanised-PD-1 mice where tumour uptake exceeded the hIgG and cold-blocked groups. Direct tier (the labelled drug binding its target in vivo). Product in model: the tracer is toripalimab itself.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour uptake of 124I-toripalimab above background (mouse %ID/g vs patient SUVmax 0.2-4.7, not commensurable)
engagement.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only (Clin Nucl Med). Eight of 11 patients had melanoma; the readout is not tumour-type specific. In mice, cold antibody lowered tumour uptake; in patients a 5 mg cold co-injection raised tumour uptake by clearing the splenic sink, a dose-level difference, not a reversal. No ClinicalTrials.gov record found (queries 124I-JS001, toripalimab PET); ChiCTR not searched.
engagement.model: Humanised-PD-1 C57BL/6 mouse with S180 homografts, 124I-toripalimab immuno-PET
engagement.note: First-in-human 124I-toripalimab PET (8 melanoma, 3 urologic patients): every tumour lesion took up tracer, spleen high, as the humanised-PD-1 mouse showed.
engagement.short: Tracer uptake in all patient tumours
engagement.quote: All primary and metastatic tumor lesions in 11 patients demonstrated different levels of uptake of 124I-JS001 with SUVmax ranging from 0.2 to 4.7.
engagement.reason: Tumour tracer uptake translated to patients
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: the clinical abstract calls itself a 'pilot clinical translation' of the mouse work (same Peking group, Sheng and Yang on both) but gives no side-by-side numbers, so comparison_stated is false. The model's prediction, that the labelled antibody localises to PD-1-expressing tumour and lymphoid tissue, held in all 11 patients, with high splenic uptake as in mice. Direction only: mouse %ID/g and patient SUVmax are not commensurable, and the cold-antibody blocking ran the opposite way at the 5 mg human dose. Engagement, not efficacy: no uptake-versus-response comparison was made, so prediction_level stays class.

considered_not_added: Fu 2017 cynomolgus PK/ADA (repeat 10 mg/kg lost exposure to ADA) vs Tang 2019 patient ADA (3/36 neutralising, accelerated clearance, all three progressed): a dose-side comparison on the existing tori-cynomolgus-monkey track, not a new system; left for the draft.

Pucotenlimab HuGEMM human-PD-1 knock-in C57BL/6 MC38 model (Zhang 2020, mAbs; TGI 93%/90% at 5/10 mg/kg vs 85% pembrolizumab): the same system as the draft's tori-hpd1-knockin-mc38-mouse track (Nanjing knock-in, exon 2+3 chimera, vs Junshi's exon 2 swap). Its comparison with Cui 2023 (NCT04749485, ORR 20.17%, primary met) is a 2023 same entry for that track; the draft's efficacy judgement wrongly says pucotenlimab has 'no published pre-clinic model'.

Pucotenlimab cynomolgus single-dose PK/ADA (Zhang 2020: ADA in 50-83% of monkeys with accelerated terminal elimination) set beside one ADA case in the phase 1a (CTR20180125) in the same paper, a stated comparison showing the monkey over-predicted immunogenicity: the cynomolgus system is already tracked (tori-cynomolgus-monkey) and this is dose-side; left for the draft.

Toripalimab in-vitro PD-1 affinity and human T-cell potency vs nivolumab/pembrolizumab (PMID 38400933, Cancer Immunol Immunother 2024): a retrodiction of PD-L1-independent benefit in NPC, NSCLC and ESCC, not melanoma, on the same in-vitro human T-cell system as the draft's tori-human-tcell-ro-invitro track.

Prolgolimab before Gordeev 2024: title/abstract search for BCD-100/prolgolimab with preclinical terms returns only Gordeev 2024 and its author correction; no earlier published model (agrees with the checker).

Pucotenlimab Bayesian/machine-learning heterogeneity and combination-regimen analysis (Cancer Med 2026, PMID 42043855) and the FDA review's toripalimab population-PK simulations: fitted to patient data, not preclinical or in-silico models that predicted patients.
Patient-derived organoids exposed to toripalimab in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (PMID 36544542): not melanoma; no melanoma organoid, PDX or co-clinical comparison for any member found.
HX009 (PD-1 x CD47 bispecific) preclinical models and nivolumab/pembrolizumab as positive controls in 34885_IVHU, TR003 and the HuGEMM study: class context, not members, not scored.

Tang 2019 peripheral activated-CD8+ null ('no major impact') as a scored engagement comparison for the PBMC-engrafted NSG track: not scored, see that entry's judgement; a checker may score it same at low confidence.

Tumour-type caveat: the PBMC-engrafted NSG efficacy arms used MC38 (toripalimab) and HCC827 (pucotenlimab), neither melanoma, like the draft's knock-in MC38 track; scored direction-only against melanoma ORR primaries.

gaps.detail: Changes nothing scored: an extra patient trial with the status unchanged. tori-hpd1-knockin-mc38-mouse efficacy is already same from 2020 (draft efficacy 2) with a later same/strengthens in 2026 (draft efficacy 4), so a 2023 pucotenlimab same leaves every year's status as is (and appended after the 2026 entry it breaks the track's year order in lint). Re-opened both sources: Zhang 2020 (PMC7153830) 'HuGEMM with human PD-1 gene knock-in syngeneic MC38-bearing mice ... HX008 significantly inhibits tumor growth'; Cui 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12885-022-10473-y, epub 2023-02-06, NCT04749485 registered 2021-02-11) 'the primary endpoint of this study was reached' (ORR 20.17%). Belongs as a patient_trials item on draft efficacy 2 (model_src doi:10.1080/19420862.2020.1724751), and that entry's judgement sentence 'no published pre-clinic model' for pucotenlimab is wrong (text only).

gaps.lead: Pucotenlimab cynomolgus single-dose PK/ADA vs phase 1a CTR20180125 (Zhang 2020)
gaps.detail: Changes nothing scored: Zhang 2020 (PMC7153830) sets monkey ADA beside 1/30 phase 1a ADA but itself says 'ADA responses in animals are not predictive of responses in humans'; the monkey PK states no human exposure, regimen target or margin, so a cynomolgus dose entry would be untested (no_prediction). Immunogenicity is not a harm scored in safety; the cynomolgus safety track is already contra (toripalimab 2019).
